questions.q: What is the author's main argument?
options: Wise handling of money through thrift builds character and independence
Money is a trifling matter that philosophers should hold in contempt
Borrowing freely is the surest key to prosperity for working men
Governments must tax the working classes more to fund thrift schemes
questions.explain: The text says how one uses money tests wisdom and stresses frugality and self-denial.

questions.q: What did Lord John Russell say working people spent more on than the government taxed them?
questions.explain: He said the Government dare not tax them as much as they tax themselves through drink.

questions.q: Who is quoted as saying the world is divided into savers and spenders?
questions.explain: Cobden told Huddersfield working men that the thrifty built civilization and spendthrifts were their slaves.

questions.q: Where and when did Mr. Bright address working men?
questions.explain: Bright spoke to an assembly of working men at Rochdale in 1847.

questions.q: What does the author imply about reform?
options: Parliamentary reform is the best cure for bad times
Personal reform is harder than reforming Church and State
questions.explain: He says it is easier to reform Church and State than our own bad habits.
